plants.name: Prunus × yedoensis
plants.description: A graceful ornamental tree that covers its bare branches in clouds of pale pink to nearly white five-petaled flowers before the leaves emerge. It is the most widely planted cherry for hanami festivals and urban avenues.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late March to mid April in temperate Northern Hemisphere regions
plants.location: Japan, Washington D.C. (USA), Korea, and temperate parks and gardens worldwide
plants.funFact: All Yoshino cherry trees are thought to descend from a single original tree propagated by grafting, which is why trees in a region often bloom in near-perfect synchrony.

plants.name: Narcissus pseudonarcissus
plants.description: A hardy bulbous perennial with trumpet-shaped yellow flowers surrounded by paler yellow petals. It carpets woodlands and meadows in early spring and is the ancestor of many garden daffodils.
plants.bloomingSeason: March to April in Northern Hemisphere temperate zones
plants.location: Western Europe, including the UK, France, and Spain; widely naturalized in North America
plants.funFact: All parts of the daffodil contain toxic alkaloids, and one of them, galantamine, is used in medicine to treat symptoms of Alzheimer's disease.

plants.name: Cercis canadensis
plants.description: A small deciduous tree whose clusters of magenta-pink, pea-like flowers burst directly from branches and even the trunk before heart-shaped leaves appear. It is a favorite of early-season pollinators.
plants.location: Eastern and central United States, northern Mexico; cultivated in gardens worldwide
plants.funFact: The redbud flowers on old wood, a trait called cauliflory, and its blossoms are edible, with a mildly tangy flavor often added to salads.

plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: A large tree with fern-like leaves that produces dense panicles of trumpet-shaped lavender-blue flowers. In the Southern Hemisphere, some trees keep blooming into early autumn, and trees in the tropics may flower sporadically.
plants.bloomingSeason: Spring in the Northern Hemisphere tropics; late bloom and rebloom in some Southern Hemisphere regions
plants.location: South America (native to Argentina and Bolivia), widely planted in Mexico, Florida, India, and Australia
plants.funFact: A carpet of fallen jacaranda blossoms is so iconic in Pretoria, South Africa, that the city is nicknamed the Jacaranda City.
